latency_ms.note: per-document render latency — a DIFFERENT quantity from throughput

image.note: measured on 2025.11.5, the current render path. Throughput is 43% BELOW the 2025.11.1 row (167,636 vs 292,826) despite the same Linode plan, the same region and a byte-identical corpus. That gap is the HOST, not the software: an A/B of the 2025.11.1, .3 and .5 images on one identical machine put all three within ~3% of each other (licensed 3,000-doc runs at workers=4, and unlicensed 480-doc runs to reach 2025.11.1, which predates the ci-2026-2 trust anchor and cannot be run licensed). So the 2025.11.2 render-path change costs nothing measurable. This is the third instance of 'Dedicated 4 vCPU' we have measured and the third distinct number (194,347 / 292,826 / 167,636) -- the plan name does not pin the silicon, which is exactly why the methodology, corpus hash and digest are the invariants rather than the absolute figure. Published without a worker sweep, so the site's scaling curve stops at the core count.

box: Linode Dedicated 8 GB (4 dedicated vCPU), eu-central (Frankfurt)
